A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF LA HABRA RECOMMENDING THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE DESIGN REVIEW 15-02 FOR THE REHABILITAITON AND EXPANSION OF THE EXISTING OFFICE BUILDINGS AT 110 AND 120 EAST LA HABRA BOULEVARD, MAKING THE APPROPRIATE FINDINGS, AS PER THE APPROVED PLANS, AND SUBJECT TO CONDITIONS.
The Planning Commission of the City of La Habra does hereby resolve as follows:

a. Town Center Office La Habra, LLC filed an application on behalf of the City of La Habra requesting Design Review 15-02 to rehabilitate and expand the existing office buildings at 110 and 120 East La Habra Boulevard.
a. T

b. This project was reviewed pursuant to the guidelines of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and determined to be Categorically Exempt pursuant to Section 15301(b), Class 1: “Existing Facilities” of the California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines.
b. T

c. The proposal has been reviewed pursuant to the requirements of the City’s National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Municipal Permit, the Local Implementation Plan (LIP), and the Model Water Quality Management Plan (WQMP); Section 7.2 Since no new imperious area is being created, this project is exempted by the Water Quality Ordinance from preparation of a Non-Priority Plan.
c. T

d. The Planning Commission held a duly noticed public hearing on February 9, 2015, to consider the applicant’s request of Design Review 15-02. The Planning Commission, after considering all the written and oral evidence offered including the staff report and all attachments, approves the request.
d. T
Section 2.

a. The applicant has succeeded in meeting their burden of providing evidence to support the granting of the Design Review application. The Planning Commission hereby makes the following required findings of the Design Review pursuant to Chapter 18.68.050.A of the La Habra Municipal Code:
1. The

The subject site is designated as “Commercial Professional/Office Priority (1.5 FAR)” by the General Plan 2035 and is improved with two interconnected office buildings. The project entails enclosure of the

courtyard, exterior façade improvement and minor interior alterations. The project complies with the goals and policies of the La Habra General Plan 2035, specifically policies LU 3.3 (A Vigorous and Active Downtown), LU 3.7 (Buildings that Engage the Street), LU 4.1 (Development Compatibility), LU 4.4 (Design Review), LU 4.5 (Community Maintenance), LU 5.2 (Sustainable Building Practices), LU 5.3 (Existing Building Reuse), LU 5.5 (Revitalization of Obsolete and Underused Properties), LU 5.6 (Building Rehabilitation), LU 13.4 (A Pedestrian-Active Downtown), LU 17.7 (Design of Civic Buildings and Spaces), LU 17.8 (Compatibility of Public Buildings and Sites), CI 2.1 (Unique Sense of Place), and CI 2.4 (Iconic Buildings). Therefore, the proposal is consistent with the City’s General Plan.

2. The proposed plan is consistent with the City's Zoning Ordinance. The subject site is zoned SP – 1 “La Habra Boulevard Specific Plan”. Pursuant to Section 18.44.050.F of the La Habra Municipal Code, Design Review is required for all major remodels in the SP -1 zone. The project entails enclosure of the courtyard, modification to the exterior façade, and minor interior alterations. The proposed modifications are consistent with the requirements of Section 18.44.060 “Design Guidelines” of La Habra Boulevard Specific Plan and therefore consistent with Section 18.44.050.F of the City’s Zoning Ordinance.

3. The proposed plan is in the best interest of the public health, safety, and welfare of the community. The design guidelines within the La Habra Boulevard Specific Plan (Section 18.44.060) were established in order to ensure that buildings, structures, signs, and landscape improvements are in harmony with other improvements, both on the site and in the vicinity of the proposed project. The project achieves these objectives and is architecturally compatible with the other buildings within area including the Community Center, Brio, Euclid/La Habra Center and the Child Care Center. Conditions of approval have been placed on the project to ensure that the public health, safety, and welfare are maintained such as conforming to relevant fire, building, and safety codes. Therefore, the proposed plan is in the best interest of the public and the community.

4. The nature of the proposed land uses and the design is appropriate for the proposed location and is compatible to the surrounding land uses and improvements.
4. The

The site is developed as an integrated part of the overall downtown. The proposed relocation of the City Hall is appropriate in the context of the overall downtown and location of government building and compatible with the permitted uses in this zone. Therefore, the
proposed project is compatible with the location and surrounding land uses and improvements.

This project was reviewed pursuant to the guidelines of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and determined to be Categorically Exempt pursuant to Section 15301(b), Class 1: “Existing Facilities” of the California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines.

The applicant/developer shall comply with all the applicable California/La Habra Building Code requirements and obtain all required permits from the Chief Building Official. Construction shall comply with the Current California/La Habra Building Code (or Residential Code), California/La Habra Plumbing Code, California/La Habra Mechanical Code, California/La Habra Electrical Code, California/La Habra Energy Code, and California/La Habra Green Building Standards Code, as applicable. All plans submitted for building permits must demonstrate intent to comply with California/La Habra Codes to the satisfaction of the Chief Building Official.
